elements.element: Customer owns Deliverables and work product created for Customer.
elements.evidence: Retained 10.4: "Any writing or work of authorship created by M&I in the course of performing the Services under this Agreement, even if paid for by Customer, shall be the property of M&I ('Developed Software')." Ownership stays with the Vendor; the redline deliberately does not reverse it.

elements.element: Vendor assigns the Deliverables and work product to Customer.
elements.evidence: No assignment language anywhere; new 10.5 grants only a licence ("M&I grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free license...").

elements.element: Vendor retains its pre-existing intellectual property.
elements.evidence: 10.4 ("All programs (including ideas and know-how and concepts) developed by M&I are and shall remain M&I's sole property") and 17.2 ("Customer acknowledges that it has no rights in any software, systems, documentation... provided by M&I") leave Vendor IP with M&I.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Vendor IP embedded in Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: 10.5 licenses "the Developed Software" only; M&I's other/pre-existing software, systems and documentation remain governed by 17.2, which still limits Customer's use to "during the Term to process its data." No perpetual licence to Vendor IP embedded in a deliverable is granted.

elements.element: Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: Same defect: 10.5's irrevocability attaches to Developed Software, not to embedded M&I pre-existing IP, whose use remains Term-limited under 17.2.

elements.element: Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: No royalty-free grant covering embedded Vendor IP; 10.5's royalty-free wording is confined to the Developed Software.

elements.element: Customer retains all rights in Customer Data.
elements.evidence: 17.1 untouched: "Customer shall remain the sole and exclusive owner of all Customer Data and other Confidential Information."

elements.element: Any Vendor licence in Customer Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services.
elements.evidence: 17.4 as amended: "provided that M&I shall use Customer Data solely to provide the Services," which carves Customer Data out of the broader "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" permission.

elements.element: The parties do not jointly own intellectual property.
elements.evidence: Condition does not arise: no joint-ownership language exists in 10.4, 10.5, 17.1, 17.2 or 17.4; ownership is allocated exclusively (M&I programs/Developed Software; Customer Data to Customer).

elements.element: Vendor may retain ownership of generic tools and know-how.
elements.evidence: Retained 10.4: "All programs (including ideas and know-how and concepts) developed by M&I are and shall remain M&I's sole property."

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: New 10.5: "perpetual... license to use, modify and sublicense the Developed Software"; 17.2 conformed with "except as expressly licensed to Customer under Section 10.5," so the Term limit no longer overrides it.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: 10.5 expressly states "irrevocable"; no retained termination or revocation hook applies to the 10.5 grant after the 17.2 conforming edit.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is worldwide.
Customer's licence to Deliverables is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: 10.5: "royalty-free"; the 10.4 refund/credit mechanic is untouched and imposes no charge for the licence.

elements.element: Customer may use and modify Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: 10.5: "license to use, modify and sublicense the Developed Software for Customer's business."

elements.element: Customer may sublicense Deliverables for its business.
Any Vendor licence in Customer Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services.
elements.evidence: 17.4 proviso: "provided that M&I shall use Customer Data solely to provide the Services," narrowing the retained "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" standard as applied to Customer Data.

reasons: Fallback checklist is complete: the inserted Section 10.5 supplies every licence attribute (perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, use/modify/sublicense for Customer's business) over the defined "Developed Software", which is the deliverable term used in 10.4; 10.4's retained sentence preserves Vendor ownership of generic programs and know-how; and the 17.4 proviso confines M&I's Customer Data use to providing the Services.

Preferred level is not reached and is not claimed: 10.4 still vests ownership of paid-for work product in M&I with no assignment, and no licence to Vendor IP embedded in deliverables is granted (17.2 still limits use of M&I software/documentation to "during the Term to process its data" outside the 10.5 carve-out).

Minimality holds: three targeted operations, each necessary — a concise new grant (a missing clause, so new words are acceptable), a conforming carve-out in 17.2 needed to remove the contradictory Term-limited "no rights" acknowledgement, and a narrow Customer Data proviso in 17.4 where the broad "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" permission sits. No survival tails, expense language, extra damages categories or unrelated deletions were added; 10.4's refund/credit mechanic and 17.1's ownership sentence are preserved intact.

Intent preserved: the cross-reference to Section 10.5 resolves to the newly numbered clause, no defined term is orphaned, and M&I's retained right to make Developed Software available to other customers and the associated refund/credit mechanic survive without contradiction (the fallback seeks a licence, not exclusivity).

Non-blocking drafting caution the drafter may wish to verify: the rationale references an Article 23 source-code licence that bars sublicensing; if that clause addresses the same subject matter as Developed Software rather than only IBS Software, add "Notwithstanding Section 17.2 and Article 23" or a corresponding conforming edit so the sublicense right in 10.5 is not read down.
